title: Getting started with halosimr
text: Generate schedule stream events. schedule_type = "3/7 Day" gives provider three day-shifts per seven-day week; rate = 0.1 means 0.1 HALO events per day, roughly 36 across year. "Random" schedule type draws day empirical Day, Night, weights reported Code Blue Blindspots paper (Day = 0.246, Night = 0.230, = 0.524). Pass weights override, example weights = c(d = 1/3, n = 1/3, o = 1/3) equal split.
code: sched <- generate_schedule(   n_providers = 200, n_days = 365,   schedule_type = "3/7 Day", seed = 42 ) ev <- generate_events(n_days = 365, rate = 0.1, seed = 42)  dim(sched)         # providers x days; cells "d" (Day), "n" (Night), "o" (Off) #> [1] 200 365 head(ev)           # one row per event #>   day_idx       date shift_type #> 1      10 2024-01-11      night #> 2      16 2024-01-17        day #> 3      22 2024-01-23        day #> 4      22 2024-01-23      night #> 5      31 2024-02-01      night #> 6      41 2024-02-11      night

title: Getting started with halosimr
text: halo_sim() bundles inputs configuration; hsrun() executes pipeline attaches results. readiness model reads parameters: exponential uses readiness_half_life_days (days readiness halve). readiness_threshold_days separate decay curve; sets gap length considered long, used flag . summary gives average readiness among -shift providers share providers least one gap longer readiness_threshold_days, flag went dangerously long without exposure. results_df summarises provider’s gaps (day-counts consecutive exposures). Key columns n_events (exposures window), gap_max (longest gap), max_gap_exceeds_threshold (whether longest gap ran past threshold): proportion_ready_on_shift, daily mean readiness across providers working day, primary outcome.
code: sim <- halo_sim(   sched, ev,   readiness_model = "exponential",   readiness_half_life_days = 60,   readiness_threshold_days = 90 ) sim <- hsrun(sim) sim #> <halo_sim>  200 providers x 365 days #>   readiness: exponential   training: none #>   mean on-shift readiness: 0.637 #>   providers exceeding gap threshold: 89.0% head(sim$results_df) #>   provider_id n_events t2first gap_min gap_q25 gap_median gap_mean gap_q75 #> 1       P0001        5      48      18   25.25       41.5 60.66667   54.75 #> 2       P0002        8      16       2   16.00       28.0 40.44444   53.00 #> 3       P0003        8      45      11   22.00       45.0 40.44444   49.00 #> 4       P0004        7      16       6   10.25       30.5 45.50000   78.50 #> 5       P0005        6     105       1   21.00       38.0 52.00000   82.50 #> 6       P0006        8      16       3   18.00       29.0 40.44444   57.00 #>   gap_max max_gap_exceeds_threshold #> 1     184                      TRUE #> 2     129                      TRUE #> 3      79                     FALSE #> 4     118                      TRUE #> 5     118                      TRUE #> 6     107                      TRUE

title: Getting started with halosimr
text: single run reflects one random draw events, curve noisy. hsrunmc() repeats run n different random seeds summarises day--day spread: median readiness across runs, plus shaded band 10th--90th-percentile range. seed needs fresh schedule events, instead fixed inputs pass two functions take seed build inputs run. training program set, hsrunmc() also runs untrained baseline arm reports lift readiness: per-day gain trained arm baseline.  trained band sits baseline; mc$lift per-day difference median readiness.
code: mc <- hsrunmc(   n = 30,   schedule_fn = function(s) generate_schedule(200, 365, "3/7 Day", seed = s),   events_fn   = function(s) generate_events(365, rate = 0.1, seed = s),   readiness_model = "exponential", readiness_half_life_days = 60,   training_program = "monthly" ) mc #> <halo_mc>  30 runs x 365 days #>   training: monthly #>   baseline median readiness: 0.671 #>   trained median readiness:  0.779  (mean lift +0.108) plot_mc_band(mc)

text: Simulate exposure high-acuity, low-occurrence (HALO) events across provider population, model readiness decays exposures, estimate training programs change . R implementation extending methodology Code Blue Blindspots paper (PMID 41633464).

title: HALO Event Exposure and Training Simulation
text: Repeat many random draws see spread, compare training program baseline:
code: library(halosimr)  # 1. Generate a schedule and a stream of HALO events sched <- generate_schedule(n_providers = 200, n_days = 365,                            schedule_type = "3/7 Day", seed = 42) ev    <- generate_events(n_days = 365, rate = 0.1, seed = 42)  # 2. Run one simulation sim <- halo_sim(sched, ev, readiness_model = "exponential",                 readiness_half_life_days = 60) sim <- hsrun(sim) sim  plot_readiness(sim) plot_gap_distribution(sim) mc <- hsrunmc(   n = 50,   schedule_fn = function(s) generate_schedule(200, 365, "3/7 Day", seed = s),   events_fn   = function(s) generate_events(365, rate = 0.1, seed = s),   readiness_model = "exponential", readiness_half_life_days = 60,   training_program = "monthly" ) mc plot_mc_band(mc)

title: HALO Event Exposure and Training Simulation
text: Four decay models map days since last exposure training reset readiness value range 0 1: binary: ready within threshold, otherwise exponential: halves every readiness_half_life_days ebbinghaus: forgetting curve 1 / (1 + b * days) step: full, partial, zero across two thresholds

halosimr 0.1.0
text: First public release. R implementation HALO event exposure readiness/training simulation, extending methodology Code Blue Blindspots paper (PMID 41633464). Single-run engine: halo_sim() hsrun(). Monte Carlo ensembles baseline vs training lift: hsrunmc(). Input generators: generate_schedule(), schedule_from_pattern(), generate_events(), plus CSV / data-frame ingest via load_schedule() load_events(). Four readiness models: readiness_binary(), readiness_exponential(), readiness_ebbinghaus(), readiness_step(). Scheduled training programs: monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, custom. Figures: plot_readiness(), plot_gap_distribution(), plot_exposure_histogram(), plot_mc_band(). Report template (inst/report_template.Rmd) getting-started vignette. Zero hard dependencies (base R ; ggplot2 optional plots). Verified reproduce Python halosim engine deterministic computation (exposure, gap statistics, readiness kernels).
